title: Interaction Field Matching: Overcoming Limitations of Electrostatic Models
claim: Prior field-based transfer has complex, curved, backward-looping field lines outside the plates; our generalized interaction yields straight, direct lines.
layout: 2 panels side by side, left prior vs right ours, shared 3D plate setup
description: Two side-by-side 3D sketches of the same setup: two parallel plates at z=0 and z=L along a z-axis, each carrying a blob-shaped distribution. In panel (a), Electrostatic Field Matching, the blobs are red and blue. Many solid arrowed field lines curve between the plates. Dotted lines loop around the outside, behind and below the plates, including backward-oriented ones, and the field E(x̃) is labeled. Panel (b), Interaction Field Matching (ours), has a gray blob on the left plate and a yellow blob on the right plate. Nearly straight parallel arrows run directly from one plate to the other, with no outside loops. Distribution labels P and Q appear under the plates. The eye goes first to the tangled red-blue panel, then to the clean straight lines in the right panel.
caption: Electrostatic Field Matching [ref] and our Interaction Field Matching (IFM) concepts. Two $D$-dimensional distributions $\mathbb{P}(\cdot)$, $\mathbb{Q}(\cdot)$ are placed in $\mathbb{R}^{D+1}$ at $z=0$ and $z=L$ (a) In EFM, the distributions are interpreted as charges creating a capacitor-like electric field. Movement along these field lines transfers the distributions, but requires consideration of all directions of the field lines. (b) Our IFM is a generalization of the EFM to arbitrary interactions between charges. One possible realization of IFM is motivated by the strong interaction between quarks. This realization does not have backward-oriented lines and has a smaller curvature of lines.
abstract: Electrostatic field matching (EFM) has recently appeared as a novel physics-inspired paradigm for data generation and transfer using the idea of an electric capacitor. However, it requires modeling electrostatic fields using neural networks, which is non-trivial because of the necessity to take into account the complex field outside the capacitor plates. In this paper, we propose Interaction Field Matching (IFM), a generalization of EFM which allows using general interaction fields beyond the electrostatic one. Furthermore, inspired by strong interactions between quarks and antiquarks in physics, we design a particular interaction field realization which solves the problems which arise when modeling electrostatic fields in EFM. We show the performance on a series of toy and image data transfer problems. Our code is available at https://github.com/justkolesov/InteractionFieldMatching
